newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's ESB 1996 operating profit 132 mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's ESB 1996 operating profit 132 mln punts.

text.p: Ireland's Electricity Supply Board (ESB) on Thursday announced profits of 132 million Irish pounds for 1996 on turnover up 69 million to 1,095 million.

"1996 was a pivotal year for the ESB. The strategies pursued over previous years yielded a strong operating performance and further steps were taken to position the company for the future," ESB Chief Executive, Joe Moran, said.
McCann said that one of the factors helping the strong performance was the growth in demand for electricity which rose 6.9 percent in electricity unit sales.
It said almost 35,000 new customers were connected by year end, the highest figure since the days of the Rural Electrification Scheme in Ireland in the 1950's.
The ESB said over the next five years it would spend 1,000 million punts on upgrading and refurbishing the electricity networks throughout the country.

It said this level of investment was essential to ensure that the company's customers continue to have a reliable and quality electricity supply to meet the needs of industry, agriculture and business.
The ESB said payroll and other savings for 1996 amounted to 36 million Irish pounds while borrowings were reduced by a further 110 million punts and at year-end stood at 825 million.
It said the balance sheet strengthened with gearing now at a satisfactory 50 percent.
EBS International, its consultancy unit, had a good year with turnover reaching 70 million punts, it said.
